job.style: a news-style report about a real-world situation

response.passage: Archaeologists recently discovered a massive stone pillar in Odisha, believed to be a site linked to the ancient Kalinga War. This discovery sheds light on how Emperor Ashoka transformed after witnessing the immense suffering caused by his conquest of the powerful Kalinga kingdom. Unlike the common myth that Kalinga was a tiny, weak village, historical evidence shows it was a formidable state that resisted the Mauryan army fiercely. After the war, Ashoka stopped seeking expansion through violence. Instead, he promoted 'Dhamma,' a set of moral principles focused on kindness and respect, which he encouraged people to follow voluntarily rather than by force. To spread these teachings, he did not use paper, which did not exist for this purpose then. Instead, he ordered his officials to carve his edicts onto polished stone pillars and rock surfaces. These inscriptions served as permanent public notices for his subjects. While many believe Chanakya was the emperor, historical records clarify that he was actually the brilliant advisor and mentor who helped Chandragupta Maurya establish the empire. These stone records remain a testament to a ruler who shifted from a conqueror to a teacher of peace, ensuring his message reached the common people across his vast lands.
response.summary: The discovery of an ancient stone pillar reveals how Emperor Ashoka shifted from violent conquest to promoting peace through Dhamma. It also clarifies that Ashoka used stone inscriptions, not paper, to communicate his moral teachings to the public.
